methods.label: Count original edges and cut-face edges
methods.explanation:
Separate the edges of \(R\) according to how they arise. Cutting off the vertices shortens each original edge at both ends, leaving one middle segment. The nonintersecting cuts therefore leave \(100\) edges of this first type.

Now let \(d_k\) be the number of original edges meeting at vertex \(V_k\). The cut at \(V_k\) creates a face with one vertex on each of those \(d_k\) edges. This face is a \(d_k\)-sided polygon, so it contributes \(d_k\) new edges.

To find the total contribution, count pairs consisting of an original edge and one of its endpoints. Counting by vertices gives \(d_1+\cdots+d_n\). Counting by edges gives \(2\cdot100\), since every edge has exactly two endpoints. Hence
\[
d_1+\cdots+d_n=200.
\]
The new cut faces are disjoint because their planes do not intersect on or inside \(Q\), so none of their edges is counted twice. Every edge of \(R\) either is a shortened original edge or bounds one of these new faces. Thus
\[
100+200=\boxed{300},
\]
which is choice \(\boxed{\text{C}}\).
methods.levelReason: Uses elementary polyhedron structure and a direct count of the two endpoints of every edge.

review.mathematicalCheck: The cuts leave 100 shortened original edges. A vertex incident to d edges creates a d-sided cut face. Counting original edge-endpoint incidences gives a total of 200 sides across the cut faces. These faces are disjoint, and every remaining edge belongs to exactly one of the two counted types, so R has 300 edges.
